{{Quote|Jedi Master Sifo-Dyas is still a leading member of the Jedi Council, is he not?''"<br />"''Master Sifo-Dyas was killed almost ten years ago.|[[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] [[Prime Minister (Kamino)|Prime Minister]] [[Lama Su/Legends|Lama Su]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
'''Sifo-Dyas''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who served the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the final decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. When the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] were revealed to have returned during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Master Sifo-Dyas secretly commissioned the creation of a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] army, placing an order with the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] government before he was betrayed and murdered by his friend, Count [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. Sifo-Dyas was extremely gifted in the Force power of [[Precognition|foresight]] and he earned a seat on the [[Jedi High Council]] prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo]]. He also carried [[Sifo-Dyas's lightsaber/Legends|two]] lightsabers [[Grievous' first lightsaber/Legends|one]] of which became the first [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] of General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]].

==Biography==
===Jedi Master===
{{Quote|They say a Master Sifo-Dyas placed an order for a clone army at the request of the Senate almost ten years ago. I was under the impression he was killed before that. Did the Council ever authorize the creation of a clone army?''"<br />"''No. Whoever placed that order did not have the authorization of the Jedi Council.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Mace Windu|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
[[File:SifoDyasCasket.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Dooku delivers Sifo-Dyas' body.]]
A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] gifted with [[Force vision/Legends|precognition]], Sifo-Dyas hailed from the [[Cassandran Worlds/Legends|Cassandran Worlds]]<ref name="TEGtW" /> and was [[Jedi training/Legends|raised]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Like most of the Jedi of his time, he was inducted into the Order at a very young age and was taught the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] at the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> Sifo-Dyas constructed his own blue-bladed [[Grievous' first lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]<ref name="EOR" /> and eventually attained the rank of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]. He became a close friend of Master [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and the two were often seen in public together.<ref name="Darth P">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Master Sifo-Dyas was chosen to sit on the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], but was removed from that position at some point prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Blockade of Naboo]] because his ideas were judged to be too extreme by the other members.<ref name="TLO" />

In [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]], Master Sifo-Dyas accompanied Dooku, Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], and Jedi High Council member [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]] to a meeting on the world of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]]. After four hours of rigorous debate, a brief recess was called, and the Jedi were confronted by [[Damask Holdings/Legends|Damask Holdings]] magister [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask]], in reality, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Plagueis, who was attempting to look for flaws in the Jedi Order he could exploit as part of his agenda. Damask aired his concerns for the future of the Republic, and both Dooku and Sifo-Dyas responded to this with their own concerns. Sifo-Dyas was quite stern with his answers and reluctant to agree with what both Dooku and Damask seemed to agree on. Sometime after, Sifo-Dyas and Dooku were present at the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]] and met [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], in reality, Damask's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] (and Dooku's future master) Darth Sidious.<ref name="Darth P" />

As his friend Dooku grew disillusioned with the Jedi and the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]], Sifo-Dyas grew concerned. He became convinced that very dark times were ahead, but the Jedi Council paid little heed to his warnings. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], a gathering was hosted by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] on Coruscant. Sifo-Dyas was in attendance alongside Jedi Masters [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]], and [[Jorus C'baoth]]. Once again, Hego Damask approached Sifo-Dyas and once more he attempted to manipulate, deceive and exploit the Jedi Master by openly admitting that a growing darkness was approaching, as he stated to the Jedi twenty years before on Serenno. Sifo-Dyas agreed to Damask's claim and Damask informed him of cloners on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] that could grow an army and hold it in reserve until it was needed. The Jedi Master was at first skeptical of this, but was persuaded to think about it, while being unaware he was being manipulated and deceived by the enemy.<ref name="Darth P" />

Not long afterwards, Sifo-Dyas approached the Kaminoans and requested a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] army for the Republic. With the funds provided by Damask Holdings, Sifo-Dyas paid the Kaminoans. At around the same time, Sifo-Dyas was contacted by Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum, who knew of the Jedi Master's expertise on the criminal underworld, and given a [[Mission to Oba Diah (Sifo-Dyas)/Legends|secret mission]] to negotiate with the [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]] of [[Oba Diah/Legends|Oba Diah]]. Because the Senate committee assigned to the Pyke case wanted to keep negotiations between the galactic government and a criminal organization strictly under the table and away from the public eye, Sifo-Dyas did not inform the Jedi Council of his mission.<ref name="TLO" /> It was at around that time that Dooku resigned from the Jedi Order and fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], joining the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] as Darth Tyranus, apprentice of Darth Sidious,<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> who had recently betrayed and murdered Plagueis.<ref name="Darth P" /> Little did Sifo-Dyas know that Sidious and Tyranus had learned of his ordering the clone army and planned the steps to his demise. The first test provided to Tyranus was to betray and murder his old friend. In doing so, he would fulfill the ancient covenant that prescribed the murder of one who was close as a measure of commitment to the Sith cause. By executing the man, Tyranus would gain full control of the project for the Sith, using Sifo-Dyas as a cover.<ref name="JvS" />

Sifo-Dyas arrived on Oba Diah together with Valorum's personal assistant [[Silman/Legends|Silman]], but the secret Pyke-Republic talks were postponed, as the Jedi Council contacted Sifo-Dyas and assigned him a mission to negotiate peace talks between [[Jungle Felucian/Legends|Jungle Felucian]] tribes on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]]. However, the two men never reached their destination, as the Pykes were contacted by Tyranus. The Syndicate, wishing to gain an advantage over rival crime families, struck a deal with Tyranus, who paid them a very large sum. At Tyranus's behest, the Pykes shot down Sifo-Dyas' [[775519/Legends|Jedi T-6 shuttle 775519]] over Oba Diah. The ship crashed on the planet's [[Oba Diah moon/Legends|desert moon]]. As proof of the fulfillment of their deal, the criminals recovered the Jedi's corpse from the wreckage and turned it over to Tyranus, taking Silman&mdash;who had survived&mdash;prisoner as insurance.<ref name="TLO" />

To ensure that it ''stayed'' a secret, Tyranus erased all records of the planet Kamino from the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]],<ref name="JvS" /> along with thirty-seven additional systems, including [[Dagobah system/Legends|Dagobah]]<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> and [[Dromund system|Dromund]].<ref name="JvS" />

[[File:SifoDyas_file.png|thumb|200px|Sifo-Dyas' official file in the Republic records]]
The official records of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] on Sifo-Dyas&mdash;classified as "[[Case file 127456/Legends|File 127456]]"&mdash;told a different story. According to the file, Jedi Master Sifo-Dyas perished while trying to negotiate peace between several tribes on Felucia, adding that he was aboard a shuttle that crashed on the planet's surface. The records went on to say that his body was eventually removed by the Felucians, who treated it in accordance to their customs, providing an explanation as to why the body was never found. Sifo-Dyas' file stipulated that "much of the information surrounding his death [remained] confidential under the [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Office of the Chancellor]]," although "further investigation in the matter [might] be authorized at a future date."<ref name="TLO" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Sifo-Dyas understood. He saw the future. That is why he helped me.|Dooku, on Sifo-Dyas|<ref name="TLO" />}}
[[File:Sifodyas.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Sifo-Dyas' body postmortem]]
Instead of disposing of his old friend's body after it was handed over to him by the Pykes, [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] Dooku preserved it in a [[cryogenic hibernation capsule]] for years, until the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] initiated their plan to turn the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] warlord, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]], into a great [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] supreme strategist. Transfusing Sifo-Dyas' [[Blood/Legends|blood]] into the veins of the cyborg, Grievous would go on to become the [[Supreme Commander of the Confederation military|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]' [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|droid army]]. Once Grievous' transformation into a cyborg had been successfully completed, Dooku gave him the very special gift of Master Sifo-Dyas' own lightsaber<ref name="EOR" /> (presumably a different one than [[Sifo-Dyas's lightsaber/Legends|that]] he carried to Oba Diah, which remained in the shuttle wreckage on the Oba Diah moon).<ref name="TLO" />

Dyas had an [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|inhibitor chip]] he intended to be instilled in each Clone of the army as a safeguard against rogue Jedi. However, Sidious and Dooku retooled the chips to contain a [[Order 66/Legends|protocol]] that when activated, would force the Clones to view the Jedi as traitors to the Republic and subsequently execute them. Dooku then presented the chip to the Kaminoans and deceived them in to believing Dyas's intention. 

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], 10 years after Sifo-Dyas's death, Jedi Knight [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] investigations led him to Kamino, the source of the [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|saberdart]] that silenced [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] attempted killer [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]]. There, in [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]], Kaminoan [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] [[Lama Su/Legends|Lama Su]] told Kenobi that Sifo-Dyas had ordered the creation of a clone army at the request of the Senate, in order to help the Galactic Republic. Su was under the impression that Sifo-Dyas was a member of the Jedi Council at the time he made the order, and did not know of Sifo-Dyas's demise. Realizing that a discrepancy in the timeline may exist, Master Kenobi contacted the High Council and revealed the existence of the army.<ref name="JvS" />

Sifo-Dyas' army was eventually revealed and used at the behest of the Galactic Republic. [[Clone Wars/Legends|The conflict]] between the Separatists and the Republic was, in fact, named after it. In [[20 BBY/Legends|the third year]] of said conflict, as part of the Sith [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|illusions]] created by Darths Sidious and Tyranus's [[Dark illusion/Legends|dark side ritual]], Sifo-Dyas appeared to Yoda on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. His specter was being tortured, bound by electricity, and begging Yoda to release him. However, Yoda saw through him with his Sith eyes, causing him to merge into Sidious.<ref name="Sacrifice">{{TCW|Sacrifice (episode)}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Sifo-Dyas's army was used by the Chancellor to [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|destroy]] the Jedi Order in accordance with a [[Grand Plan/Legends|Sith plot]] a millennium in the making.<ref name="JvS" /> Chancellor Palpatine, who was revealed himself Sidious ordered the Clones to execute Order 66, his secret protocol that commanded the Clones to kill the Jedi for being traitors to the Republic. Upon the issuance of the command, their inhibitor chips activated and immediately brainwashed them into viewing the Jedi as traitors to the Republic and subsequently turning their weapons on them, leading to the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|downfall and near destruction of the Jedi Order]]. In this way, Sifo-Dyas, used, exploited, manipulated and deceived by the Sith Lords, had a hand in the destruction of the Jedi Order in his effort to save it.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Warren_fu.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Warren Fu]] was used as reference for Sifo-Dyas.]]
In early drafts of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], the name of the Jedi who contacted the Kaminoans was '''Sido-Dyas''', pointing to a likely early conceptual connection to [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. However, "Sifo-Dyas" appears in one place, apparently as a typo, that Lucas later preferred to the original name.<ref name="draftscript">{{WebCite|url=https://sfy.ru/?script=star_wars_episode_2|text=Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones (2002) movie script|work=[https://sfy.ru Screenplays for You]|archivedate=20200525051557}}</ref>

In addition, "Sido-Dyas" was originally only a false identity for Sidious&mdash;Obi-Wan Kenobi claimed never to have heard of him, and [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] confirmed that there was no Jedi by that name.<ref name="draftscript" />

His backstory was promised by [[George Lucas]] to be revealed in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}} DVD commentary</ref> However, once Lucas refocused the film's story to center on Anakin, he was forced to cut several plot points related to ''Attack of the Clones'', including Sifo-Dyas' backstory. However, he allowed author [[James Luceno]] to reveal it in the lead-in novel ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''.

The character's name was changed to '''Zaifo-Vias''' in Brazil. The original name is phonetically similar to a vulgar expletive in Brazilian Portuguese, so this was done to prevent confusion.

The first visual appearance of Sifo-Dyas was in ''[[The Eyes of Revolution]]'' comic featured in ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]''. The story was written and drawn by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] concept artist [[Warren Fu]], and as an [[Easter egg (virtual)|easter egg]], or inside joke, Fu used himself for the face of the Jedi Master. Artist [[Chris Trevas]] noticed Fu's likeness in the comic while doing research for his own illustration of Sifo-Dyas in ''[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force]]''. For the sake of continuity, and respect for a fellow artist, Trevas contacted Fu to reprise his role for the ''Jedi vs. Sith'' illustration as well.<ref name="DELREY">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jivemagazine.com/column.php?pid=23688|text=DEL REY Internet newsletter, December 2007], URL accessed on [[May 14]], [[2008]]|archivedate=20080323085443}}</ref>

In 2014, the episode "[[The Lost One]]" of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series']] [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]] unveiled more details about Sifo-Dyas's last moments and the exact manner of his death.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/life/2013/04/30/star-wars-the-clone-wars-animation/2122763|text='Clone Wars' still has life in the 'Star Wars' universe|work=USA Today|archivedate=20130501014037}}</ref>
